request.summary: Create a production-grade landscape wayfinding kiosk around the canonical Wayfinding Editor Preview renderer, preserving every authored map presentation setting while adding ordinary 2D and 3D exploration, Preview's animated authored 2D route reveal, a refined directory, live datasource status, complete exploded 3D routes, camera guidance, spoken guidance, and QR continuation on a mobile PWA.
request.audience: Visitors using a large landscape touchscreen kiosk in a campus, office, healthcare, education, or public venue.
request.primaryGoal: Let a visitor explore the ordinary authored 2D or 3D map, preview the selected route through an animated authored 2D reveal, understand the complete exploded 3D journey at a glance, and continue the same semantic route on a phone without manual step navigation or a separate Atlas mode.

assumptions: The bundled synthetic .wbmap is a deterministic harness fixture and is replaceable with any Studio-published venue package without changing kiosk composition or renderer logic.
Map geometry, labels, materials, origins, route styling, exploded-floor behavior, camera behavior, and authored voice guidance are owned by the published map and canonical viewer.
The optional DestinationStatus TABLE provides operational overlay data only and never modifies map presentation.
Spoken guidance begins only after the visitor explicitly starts or replays a route.
The mobile companion URL is a stable public PWA address; the QR contains route state and custom-app identity but never a temporary storage path.

surfaceStrategy.rationale: The requested deployment is a dedicated 16:9 landscape kiosk whose directory, switchable 2D/3D map, and destination panel are composed as one fixed visitor experience.

surfaces.purpose: Full HD landscape touchscreen kiosk with simultaneous directory, canonical 2D/3D map, and destination context.

ownership.rationale: The kiosk consumes the same renderer primitives as Editor Preview and must not reinterpret the authored .wbmap.
The production kiosk hierarchy and ergonomics remain code-owned so a map replacement cannot break the visitor experience.
Operators may identify the venue and adapt the primary visitor prompt.
Operators may replace the stable companion deployment URL without changing semantic handoff encoding or map rendering.
Operators may theme the kiosk shell; these settings never leak into the canonical map renderer.
Operational availability, wait time, and notices belong to a live TABLE keyed by stable map destination IDs.
These values describe the current visitor's temporary exploration and must not be written back to configuration or datasources.

views.purpose: Show the complete authored campus or venue with interactive buildings and labels.
Show a selected place, map-defined description or media, live operational status, and the animated authored 2D route preview.
Show the entire route across site and building floors with route reveal and camera progression.
Show a scannable QR code that transfers server, app identity, map resource, origin, destination, route profile, language, and optional datasource ID to the companion PWA.

inputs.action: Search, filter, select a destination, start or end a route, replay guidance, transfer a route to mobile, choose language, and toggle accessibility or audio.
Select map entities, pan and zoom the ordinary 2D map, or orbit and zoom the normal 3D scene.
Reach every kiosk action and manipulate the focused 2D or 3D map with documented keyboard controls.

session.expectation: The visitor can end a route or choose another destination; no route is advanced through Next or Previous steps.

rendering.rationale: A fixed Full HD canvas protects the large-touch layout and the renderer's camera framing on a dedicated landscape kiosk.

motion.rationale: The kiosk shell has no decorative page transition. Essential route reveal and camera guidance are domain behavior owned by the canonical wayfinding viewer and remain functional with reduced-motion preferences.

branding.provenance: No customer brand asset is part of the public example; the shell uses a restrained synthetic Northline identity while the map preserves its authored assets.
branding.fallback: Use the built-in dark kiosk palette and venue name settings.

settings.purpose: Sets the compact venue identity in the directory header.
Sets the stable mobile companion PWA base URL used for versioned QR handoff.
Selects the dark, light, or custom kiosk shell palette.
Sets the custom shell accent without affecting the map.
Sets custom directory and detail panel surfaces.
Sets custom supporting copy and metadata.

dynamicText.fallback: Preserve the compact identity line and ellipsize only after the available header width is exhausted.
dynamicText.rationale: The venue name is supporting identity and must not displace the search experience.

dynamicText.fallback: Use up to four readable lines and preserve the search field below it.
dynamicText.rationale: This is the visitor's primary orientation prompt at near-touch distance.

dynamicText.fallback: Preserve a compact directory row and ellipsize only after the available name width is exhausted.
dynamicText.rationale: Map-defined names vary by venue and language but must not break directory scanning.

dynamicText.fallback: Use two primary lines and preserve the route action below the description.
dynamicText.rationale: The selected destination name is the primary decision context before a visitor starts navigation.

dynamicText.fallback: Keep the status label visible and clamp the secondary operational note after three lines.
dynamicText.rationale: Live visitor notices are important but must not push the route action below the kiosk fold.

states.expectation: The complete authored site, searchable directory, and empty destination panel fill the Full HD kiosk without overflow.
The visitor can switch to the authored normal 3D projection with visible building volume, labels, markers, orbit, and zoom without entering route mode.
Selecting a routeable place reveals the map-authored route in ordinary 2D using Preview's casing, color, width, chevrons, markers, flow or pulse styling, and replayable path-drawing animation.
The selected route renders in exploded 3D with all route segments visible and no Next, Previous, or Atlas controls.
The selected destination opens a high-contrast scannable QR dialog whose link transfers semantic route state to the stable companion PWA without exposing a Wallboard storage path.
A closed datasource row shows its operational message and disables route start without altering the map scene.
The kiosk shell switches to a high-contrast light palette while the authored map presentation remains unchanged.
Custom shell palette values update visitor chrome while the canonical map keeps the published presentation.
Long venue and welcome copy stay readable and preserve directory search and map area.

behaviors.expectation: Selecting or reselecting a routeable place replays the canonical Editor Preview 2D path reveal before the visitor starts the complete 3D journey.
Starting a route shows every route segment in the canonical exploded 3D scene, reveals the full path, and arrives at a destination orbit without manual step state.
Visitor-triggered route start and replay speak the map-authored guidance in the selected language; muting cancels speech without ending the route.

The QR link carries the versioned server, custom-app identity, map resource, kiosk origin, selected destination, profile, language, and optional public datasource ID, while the phone resolves the current published resource path itself.
Live TABLE updates change status, wait time, note, and availability without rebuilding or restyling the map renderer.
The route experience exposes End route and Replay only; Atlas, Next, Previous, and step instruction cards are absent.

visualDirection.summary: A top-tier architectural visitor kiosk: calm dark shell, large authored map as the hero, precise compact controls, and destination detail that supports rather than competes with the renderer.
signatureChoices: A simultaneous directory-map-detail composition instead of modal navigation or dashboard cards.
The exact Wayfinding Editor Preview renderer owns all 2D and 3D map pixels and 3D journey behavior.
Selection reveals the authored 2D route; one subsequent visitor action launches both the complete 3D camera journey and authored spoken guidance.
A destination-specific QR dialog transfers the semantic route to the stable mobile PWA without coupling the visitor link to an upload storage ID.
avoid: Reinvented map geometry, generic 3D approximations, or shell palette values applied to map materials.
Atlas 2D mode, manual Next or Previous route steps, instruction-card timelines, or dashboard-like nested cards.

visualReview.intent: The kiosk should feel installation-ready and architecturally specific while making the published map, not the surrounding chrome, the dominant visual object.
focus: Verify map-authored polygon colors, backgrounds, labels, imagery, route styling, and transparency match the canonical viewer at overview and journey states.
Confirm selection replays the authored 2D path animation before the complete 3D journey begins.
Confirm the mobile QR dialog remains scannable at kiosk distance and names the selected destination clearly.
Confirm the exploded route remains legible across external and internal building segments while camera motion settles on the destination.
Inspect long venue, destination, and datasource copy for clipping at near-touch font floors.
Confirm dark, light, and custom shell themes never recolor the map renderer.
